name: Dimmer switch plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a switch that varies lamp brightness, drawn as a switch with an added variability arrow.
description: A dimmer varies the power delivered to luminaires using phase-cut electronics or a control signal. IEC-style plans typically draw the switch mark with an oblique arrow or a small adjustment mark to show continuous variation, and the switching line links it to the dimmed group.

Dimmer compatibility with LED drivers is a frequent site problem, so the symbol is usually backed by a schedule stating the dimming method: leading edge, trailing edge, 0-10 V or DALI. The reader should check that every luminaire on the dimmed group is dimmable by that method.
The plan mark does not state the dimming technology or minimum load. A rotary or push dimmer looks the same on the plan.
readingNotes: Check the dimming method in the schedule.
Confirm every luminaire in the group is compatible.
drawingChecklist: State dimming method and rated load.
Link to the dimmed luminaire group.
Note minimum load for LED circuits.
distinction: A one-way switch has no variability mark; the dimmer adds continuous control of light output.
